cover.title:
Sliding window,
**fixed size**
cover.lead: k numbers in a row: one number joins, one leaves, and the sum is reused.
cover.use_it_when: The question is about numbers next to each other, in a block of fixed length k.
cover.why_it_matters: It turns n × k additions into about n, and post 08 grows it into any size.
cover.promise: You'll write the window in {lines} lines.

slides.title: Watch it slide
slides.lead: The biggest sum of 3 in a row in 2 1 5 1 3 2.

slides.title: A 3-day total
slides.scene: A shop keeps a 3-day sales total. Each morning it adds today and drops the day that fell out. No one re-adds all 3.

blocks.text: New total = old total [[+ the day that joins − the day that leaves]].

slides.title: One in, one out
slides.lead: The first sum is added up once. After that, each window costs one add and one subtract.

quickcheck.question: k = 2 on 4 2 7 1. What is the biggest sum?

blocks.text: When nums[i] joins, the number k places back leaves, so the window stays exactly k long.

slides.title: Fixed window

lines: for i from k to length(nums) - 1:

slides.explain: Lines 3 and 4 add up the first window once. Line 7 slides it: one number in, one out.

slides.title: Drop the right one
slides.lead: Subtract nums[i − k + 1] and at i = 3 you remove the 1 that is still inside.

caption.first: Sliding window with a fixed size k: the biggest sum of k numbers in a row in one pass (LeetCode 643 practice).
lines: Add up the first k once. Then one number joins and nums[i − k] leaves.
The trap: drop nums[i − k + 1] and 2 1 5 1 3 2 gives 8 instead of 9.
